'''Michael Abraham''' (also '''Michael''' '''Avraham''') ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] מיכאל אברהם; born January 15, 1960) is an Israeli [[rabbi]] at [[Bar-Ilan University]]'s [[:he: המכון הגבוה לתורה|''Machon HaGavoah LeTorah'']] ("Institute of Advanced [[Torah study|Torah Studies]]") and holds a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[theoretical physics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=אברהם מיכאל {{!}} המדרשה {{!}} אוניברסיטת בר-אילן |url=https://midrasha.biu.ac.il/node/541 |access-date=2022-08-15 |website=midrasha.biu.ac.il}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Abraham was born in the city of [[Haifa]], studied in a [[Midrashiat Noam]] [[Jewish day school|yeshiva high-school]] and then at [[Yeshivat Har Etzion]]. He served in the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] as a tank commander. He went on to study in an [[Haredi Judaism|ultra-orthodox]] [[yeshiva]] in [[Bnei Brak]]. He received a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[electrical engineering]] from [[Tel Aviv University]] and a [[Master's degree|master's]] and Phd in theoretical physics from Bar-Ilan University focused on [[mesoscopic physics]]. He spent several years in the town of [[Yeruham]] teaching at the local [[Hesder]] yeshiva. Since 2012, he lives in [[Lod]] and teaches at Bar-Ilan University's Institute of Advanced Torah Studies. Abraham is married and has six children.<ref name=":0" />

== Works ==
Together with Gavriel Hazut, Avrham founded an organization called 'mida tova' focused on the use of [[Logic|formal logic]] and [[talmudical hermeneutics]] in the modern study of Torah and [[halakha]] (Jewish law). He is also part of the group in Bar-Ilan University who publish "Studies in Talmudic Logic".<ref>{{Cite web |title=College Publications - Studies |url=http://www.collegepublications.co.uk/stl/ |access-date=2022-08-15 |website=www.collegepublications.co.uk}}</ref>  Abraham authored a series of popular books analyzing the relationship between Judaism and [[postmodernism]] as well as other issues at the intersection of philosophy, religion, and science. Abraham is known as an independent thinker with unorthodox views on several controversial topics including his attitude towards [[religious dogma]] and the need to reform parts of Halakha.<ref>{{Cite web |title="אין שום דבר ביהדות חוץ מהלכה" |url=https://www.makorrishon.co.il/judaism/230815/ |access-date=2022-08-15 |website=www.makorrishon.co.il |date=24 May 2020 }}</ref>
